questions.title: How do you build fully accessible Modal dialogs (WAI-ARIA specifications)?
questions.description:
Accessible Modals

Building an accessible modal dialog is one of the most common frontend interview tasks testing deep accessibility knowledge. Simply setting absolute center alignment and backdrop opacity is insufficient.

Core Accessibility Requirements

  • Focus Trap: Tab focus must cycle only within the modal elements and cannot escape to the background document.
  • Escape Key: Pressing Escape must close the modal.
  • Focus Restoring: When the modal closes, focus must be returned to the element that triggered it.
  • ARIA Roles: Role dialog or alertdialog, aria-modal="true", and linking description/title (aria-labelledby, aria-describedby).
  • Aria-hidden: Hide background elements from screen readers using aria-hidden="true" when modal is active.
questions.bestPractices:
• Use the HTML5 native <dialog> element where possible, as it provides focus trap and escape support out-of-the-box in modern browsers.
  • If custom-implementing, use packages like Radix Dialog to avoid focus trap edge cases.
questions.commonMistakes:
• Leaving the background scrollable.
  • Allowing keyboard tab selection to wander onto background buttons, enabling actions outside the modal context.
questions.example:
// Simple hook for focus restoration and escape key
useEffect(() => {
  const originalFocus = document.activeElement;
  
  const handleKeyDown = (e) => {
    if (e.key === 'Escape') onClose();
  };
  
  window.addEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);
  return () => {
    window.removeEventListener('keydown', handleKeyDown);
    if (originalFocus) (originalFocus as HTMLElement).focus();
  };
}, [onClose]);
questions.interviewTip: Highlight focus trapping, escape-key triggers, and focus restoration as the primary challenges of modal accessibility. These three details show senior-level experience.
